peer_group_definition.reproducible_from: Sorted 2019 census county population, split into four equal-count bands.
peer_group_definition.disclaimer: Peer-group membership is a population-size classification only. It carries no implication about development performance or data quality.

performance_index_methodology.label: Published snapshot — P09 cleared the latest cross-sectional score for banded display; exact ranks remain diagnostic and longitudinal composite movement is withheld.
performance_index_methodology.inclusion_rule: Indicator has a published, non-null higher_is_better rule AND is P06 ranking-eligible (comparable, A/B/C provenance, shared period) for all 47 counties, with zero exceptions.
performance_index_methodology.domain_exclusion_reason: No indicator in this domain currently satisfies the inclusion rule for all 47 counties (most are survey estimates the Atlas taxonomy withholds from ranking due to sampling uncertainty, or lack a defensible direction rule). This is disclosed, not resolved, by this release.
performance_index_methodology.normalization: Winsorized min-max per indicator: values are clipped to the [5th, 95th] national percentile before scaling to 0–100, oriented so 100 is always the favourable end per the published direction rule.
performance_index_methodology.missing_data_policy: No imputation. An indicator not meeting the inclusion rule for all 47 counties is excluded from the index entirely rather than estimated for the counties that lack it.
performance_index_methodology.outlier_policy: Winsorization at the 5th/95th percentile bounds extreme values' influence on the 0–100 scale without discarding the observation.
performance_index_methodology.weighting_disclosure: No single weighting is asserted as correct. Three scenarios are published and a county's rank-robustness band is the range across them, not a single scenario's result.
performance_index_methodology.honest_limitation: This index currently reflects only fiscal, living, education, economic performance (5 indicators). It is NOT a comprehensive county-development index and must not be described as one — 3 domains (infrastructure, health, governance) contribute nothing because no indicator in them yet meets the inclusion rule.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

delivery_layer_methodology.title: County Fiscal Delivery & Accountability
delivery_layer_methodology.scope: A narrow public-finance construct using only directly government-linked FY2024/25 measures: budget execution, own-source-revenue target attainment and pending-bills burden. Broad social/economic outcomes are excluded from the score.

treasury_brop.source_name: National Treasury — 2025 Budget Review and Outlook Paper
treasury_brop.primary_data_agency: Office of the Controller of Budget

oag_summary.source_name: Office of the Auditor-General — Summary Report on County Governments 2023/2024

pfm_regulations.source_name: Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 — Regulation 25(1)(b)

measures_active.source_table: National Treasury 2025 BROP Table 8 / Annex Table 7

pillars_scored.construction: Mean of normalized overall and development budget absorption.
Normalized OSR target attainment, with scoring input capped at 100% while the published raw attainment remains visible.
Inverse-normalized pending bills as a share of approved budget; lower burden is better.

accountability_signals_not_scored.reason: Published as statutory compliance/non-compliance. The final source does not provide a consistently extracted exact ratio for every county, and a binary legal-compliance flag is not treated as an arbitrary cardinal score.
Published as audit context. Modified audit-opinion categories are not given arbitrary numeric distances, and exact classes are only shown where verified from the indexed OAG appendix extract.

delivery_layer_methodology.weighting: Equal one-third weight across execution, revenue mobilisation and arrears control. The two absorption measures are averaged inside the execution pillar so fiscal execution is not double-counted.
delivery_layer_methodology.normalization: Winsorized min-max at the 5th/95th percentile within the FY2024/25 county distribution. Pending-bills burden is direction-reversed after normalization. No imputation.
delivery_layer_methodology.osr_cap_policy: Raw OSR attainment above 100% remains visible, but the scoring input is capped at 100% to avoid rewarding target under-setting or overshoot beyond complete target attainment.
delivery_layer_methodology.missing_data_policy: No imputation. A county missing any scored pillar receives no overall delivery score or rank but retains all available pillar/accountability evidence. Narok is withheld from the composite because the final published pending-bills table records no submitted value.

wage_ceiling_context.statement: The final 2025 BROP states that only eight county governments adhered to the 35 percent ceiling in FY 2024/25.

audit_context.verification_note: Primary OAG Appendix 1(a) was re-checked end-to-end on 2026-08-31; all 47 County Executives are explicitly listed as Qualified.
audit_context.compatibility_note: Legacy P10 field retained as an alias to the complete 47-county primary Appendix 1(a) verification.

delivery_layer_methodology.attribution_guardrail: The layer evaluates a county government fiscal record for a specified period. It does not assign broad county outcomes to a governor and does not convert the score into a claim of personal causation.

recognition_methodology.subject: county_administration_period
recognition_methodology.attribution_statement: Administration-period presentation is a temporal comparison, not a personal causal score. No named governor is scored or credited/blamed for broad county outcomes.
recognition_methodology.performance_index_excluded: The P08/P09 development snapshot is excluded from administration recognition because P09 has not cleared it for longitudinal composite movement. P11 recognition uses only P10 fiscal/accountability evidence and directly observed fiscal change.

cycle_definition.election_source_name: Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission — 2022 General Election
cycle_definition.constitutional_basis: Constitution of Kenya, Article 180(1): county governors are elected on the same day as a general election, on the second Tuesday in August every fifth year.
cycle_definition.transition_treatment: FY2022/23 straddles the August 2022 election and administrative transition, so it is shown as context but excluded from baseline-to-current change calculations.

recognition_methodology.transition_year_policy: FY2022/23 straddles the August 2022 election and administrative transition, so it is shown as context but excluded from baseline-to-current change calculations.

recognition_rules_published.label: Current fiscal delivery leaders
recognition_rules_published.eligible: Counties with complete P10 FY2024/25 scores only.
recognition_rules_published.formula: P10 County Fiscal Delivery & Accountability score for FY2024/25.
recognition_rules_published.tie_rule: Top five positions by score; all counties tied at the fifth-place score are included.

recognition_rules_published.label: Most improved overall budget absorption this administration cycle
recognition_rules_published.eligible: All counties with FY2021/22 baseline and FY2024/25 latest values.
recognition_rules_published.formula: overall_absorption[FY2024/25] − overall_absorption[FY2021/22]. FY2022/23 is excluded as a transition year.
recognition_rules_published.tie_rule: Top five positions by percentage-point improvement; all counties tied at the fifth-place value are included.

recognition_rules_published.label: Most improved development absorption this administration cycle
recognition_rules_published.eligible: All counties with FY2021/22 baseline and FY2024/25 latest values.
recognition_rules_published.formula: development_absorption[FY2024/25] − development_absorption[FY2021/22]. FY2022/23 is excluded as a transition year.
recognition_rules_published.tie_rule: Top five positions by percentage-point improvement; all counties tied at the fifth-place value are included.

recognition_rules_published.label: Own-source-revenue target attainment leaders
recognition_rules_published.eligible: Counties with a published FY2024/25 OSR target-attainment value.
recognition_rules_published.formula: Published FY2024/25 OSR collected ÷ county OSR target × 100. Recognition uses the reported raw attainment; the P10 score itself caps this input at 100%.
recognition_rules_published.tie_rule: Top five positions by reported attainment; all counties tied at the fifth-place value are included.

recognition_rules_published.label: Lowest pending-bills burden
recognition_rules_published.eligible: Counties with a submitted FY2024/25 pending-bills value.
recognition_rules_published.formula: Published pending bills ÷ approved FY2024/25 county budget × 100.
recognition_rules_published.tie_rule: Top five positions with the lowest burden; all counties tied at the fifth-place value are included. Missing/non-submitted values are not ranked.

recognition_rules_published.label: Wage-ceiling compliance
recognition_rules_published.eligible: All counties, using the final FY2024/25 published compliance statement.
recognition_rules_published.formula: County qualifies when personnel emoluments are at or below the statutory 35% of total county revenue ceiling.
recognition_rules_published.tie_rule: No ranking. Every compliant county is shown equally.

county_recognition.label: Current fiscal delivery leaders
county_recognition.eligible: Counties with complete P10 FY2024/25 scores only.
county_recognition.formula: P10 County Fiscal Delivery & Accountability score for FY2024/25.
county_recognition.tie_rule: Top five positions by score; all counties tied at the fifth-place score are included.

county_recognition.label: Most improved overall budget absorption this administration cycle
county_recognition.eligible: All counties with FY2021/22 baseline and FY2024/25 latest values.

county_recognition.label: Most improved development absorption this administration cycle

county_recognition.formula: development_absorption[FY2024/25] − development_absorption[FY2021/22]. FY2022/23 is excluded as a transition year.
county_recognition.tie_rule: Top five positions by percentage-point improvement; all counties tied at the fifth-place value are included.

county_recognition.formula: Published FY2024/25 OSR collected ÷ county OSR target × 100. Recognition uses the reported raw attainment; the P10 score itself caps this input at 100%.
county_recognition.tie_rule: Top five positions by reported attainment; all counties tied at the fifth-place value are included.

working_well: County budget absorption rate: 77% in FY 2024/25, 82nd percentile within the peer-group (tier 4) — higher than the peer_group median of 75%.
Development budget absorption rate: 62% in FY 2024/25, 91st percentile within the peer-group (tier 4) — higher than the peer_group median of 57%.
what_changed: County budget absorption rate improved by 2.52 percentage points as of FY 2024/25 (was 74.48%, now 77%).

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

Labour-force participation rate, age 15–64: 80.1% in 2019 census, 100th percentile within the peer-group (tier 3) — higher than the peer_group median of 73.05%.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.
