release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

monetary_counterfactual.interpretation: Approved budget that would have been executed at the benchmark absorption rate, and was not.

narrative.reproducible_from: P06 ranking/trend fields and the P03 fiscal panel only; no free-form text.
working_well: Population age 3+ at school or learning institution: 46.4% in 2019 census, 83rd percentile within the peer-group (tier 1) — higher than the peer_group median of 38.25%.
needs_attention: County budget absorption rate: 70% in FY 2024/25, 17th percentile within the peer-group (tier 1) — lower than the peer_group median of 75.5%.
Development budget absorption rate: 37% in FY 2024/25, 8th percentile within the peer-group (tier 1) — lower than the peer_group median of 54.5%.
Labour-force participation rate, age 15–64: 71.6% in 2019 census, 25th percentile within the peer-group (tier 1) — lower than the peer_group median of 75.2%.
what_changed: County budget absorption rate worsened by 14.75 percentage points as of FY 2024/25 (was 84.75%, now 70%).
Development budget absorption rate worsened by 24.2 percentage points as of FY 2024/25 (was 61.2%, now 37%).

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.

administrationScorecard.subject: county_administration_period
administrationScorecard.attribution_caution: This record associates fiscal outcomes with an election-cycle administration period only. It does not claim that a named governor personally caused the changes; outcomes also reflect county assemblies, public servants, inherited obligations, national transfers, macroeconomic conditions and other factors.

release_decision.publication_statement: GO for the latest cross-sectional snapshot as a 0–100 score plus broad relative-position band. Exact rank remains diagnostic only. NO-GO for longitudinal composite movement until currently single-period inputs acquire comparable history and the historical stability gate is met.

snapshot_release.decision_rule: GO when at least two plausible full-composite weighting scenarios are available and at least 85% of counties remain in the same or an adjacent 20-percentage-point relative-position band across those scenarios.
snapshot_release.stress_scenario_reason: The fiscal-only scenario deliberately removes non-fiscal domains. It is an extreme specification stress test, not an alternative full-composite weighting, so it is disclosed separately rather than allowed to determine the snapshot publication gate.

longitudinal_release.decision_rule: GO only when every included indicator has at least two comparable observed periods and the historically reconstructable sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.80.
reasons_if_no_go: 3 of 5 included indicators (IND-RENT-BURDEN, IND-SCHOOL-ATTENDANCE-RATE, IND-LABOUR-FORCE-PARTICIPATION) have only one comparable observed period, so a historical composite cannot be reconstructed without inventing history.

The historically observable fiscal-execution sub-index has average consecutive-year Spearman rank correlation 0.43, below the pre-declared 0.80 stability threshold; year-to-year ordering is too mobile to support a strong longitudinal composite claim.

historical_backtest.interpretation: The reconstructable historical sub-index shows material year-to-year rank movement; this is evidence against publishing a strong longitudinal composite claim.

release_decision.next_review_trigger: Re-run the longitudinal gate when rent burden, school attendance and labour-force participation each have at least two methodologically comparable county observations; re-run the snapshot gate whenever the indicator set, direction rules, normalization or weighting scenarios change.

measures.cap_policy: Attainment above 100% is displayed as reported but capped at 100% for scoring so counties are not rewarded for target under-setting or target overshoot beyond full attainment.

deliveryLayer.attribution_note: This is a county-government fiscal delivery score for a stated fiscal year. It is not a personal governor score and does not claim that one office-holder caused the observed result.
